title: Trump Blasts Zelensky as Unwilling to End War Following Massive Ukrainian Strike on Russian Oil Terminal
snippet: Tensions between Washington and Kyiv escalated after President Donald Trump publicly rebuked Volodymyr Zelensky following a major Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian energy facility.
content:
Tensions between Washington and Kyiv reached a boiling point this weekend as President Donald Trump publicly lashed out at Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, claiming the leader "doesn’t want to end this war, and probably never did." The sharp rebuke came shortly after Ukrainian forces launched one of their largest drone attacks of the year, striking a major Russian oil terminal in direct defiance of White House demands.

Writing on Truth Social, Trump defended his strategy to bring Moscow to the negotiating table, which recently included invoking a controversial waiver to exempt Russia from economic penalties mandated by Congress. Trump argued that penalizing Moscow right now would disrupt sensitive peace negotiations, asserting that "great progress is being made."

Kyiv Defies Washington Demand Amid Grid Attacks

The latest rift follows an overnight barrage in which Russia's Defense Ministry claimed to intercept more than 1,000 Ukrainian drones. Despite the heavy air defense response, Ukrainian strikes successfully targeted the St. Petersburg Oil Terminal—a vital hub capable of handling 12.5 million tons of fuel annually—as well as a commercial distribution center and data infrastructure, leaving one dead and five injured.

Ukraine's continued deep strikes into Russian territory come despite explicit warnings from the Trump administration to avoid targeting energy infrastructure, a move the White House hopes will stabilize global oil and diesel markets.

Appearing on NBC's "Meet the Press," Zelensky pushed back against the administration's stance, warning that U.S. moves to ease pressure on Moscow represent a "historic mistake" and amount to "more support for Russian aggression." Zelensky pointed out that Russia has shown no signs of easing its own campaign, noting Moscow launched 76 attacks against Ukrainian energy facilities over the past week alone.

Strained Intelligence and Technological Support

The dispute underscores growing anxieties in Kyiv over the stability of American support as winter approaches. Zelensky revealed that Ukraine has faced recent operational hurdles with U.S.-supplied support, including speed restrictions placed on Starlink networks used to guide battlefield drones and temporary disruptions in critical U.S. satellite intelligence that provides early warnings for incoming Russian ballistic missiles.

Despite the increasingly tense public exchanges, Zelensky confirmed that diplomatic channels remain active. Ukrainian officials held talks on Sunday with U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff and Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner in an ongoing effort to preserve the strategic alliance.
